- **National census:** 'England and Wales, Census, 1851' (collection id 2563939, ~1.57M entries) directly covers the target year and will show the household shortly before a death, including age, birthplace, and occupation, which can corroborate identity.
- **Access:** Indexed with images, per collections_search.

### Probate and court records
- **Testate or intestate:** Determine before searching — wills go to pre-1858 ecclesiastical probate series; intestate estates to administration records of the same courts.
- **Date range/where held:** Before 11 January 1858, probate for Yorkshire was granted by ecclesiastical courts (Exchequer and Prerogative Courts of York, and local peculiars), not the later civil Principal Probate Registry. 'Yorkshire, England, Probate Records, 1521-1858' (Ancestry, https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/5246) and the 'York Peculiars Probate Index 1383-1883' (findmypast) cover this. The 1858+ 'England and Wales, National Probate Calendar' (Ancestry, https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1904) does not apply to an 1851 death.

### Land records
- **Types:** Deeds, land tax assessments. 'West Yorkshire, England, Select Land Tax Records, 1704-1932' (Ancestry, https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/5108) overlaps 1851.
- **Where held:** West Riding Registry of Deeds historically; not further confirmed by these tools.

### Military records
- Not a priority record type for an 1851 civilian death; no Yorkshire-specific military collection surfaced in this survey for the period.

### Cemetery records
- 'England, Lancashire, Oldham Cemetery Registers, 1797-2004' and similar borough cemetery registers exist for neighboring counties; no Yorkshire-specific cemetery register surfaced in collections_search for 1851, though parish burial registers (above) cover burials in this period. Check 'Yorkshire Monumental Inscriptions' (findmypast) and FindAGrave for gravestone transcriptions.

### Newspaper records
- Several Yorkshire newspapers were publishing by 1851, e.g. the Yorkshire Gazette (1819-1920, findmypast) and the Huddersfield and Holmfirth Examiner (1851-1982, findmypast) — useful for death/burial notices and inquests.

### Immigration/emigration records
- Not applicable as a primary source for an inland death record; omitted beyond noting Yorkshire has no major 1851-era port of entry relevant here.

### Tax records
- Land Tax Assessments and Electoral Registers (e.g. 'West Yorkshire, England, Electoral Registers, 1840-1962') can substitute for gaps between censuses and corroborate residence near 1851.

### Other record types
- Poor Law and workhouse records ('West Yorkshire, England Select Poor Law and Township Records, 1663-1914') may record a pauper's death and burial if applicable.

## Records NOT online
- The GRO death certificate itself (only the index is online; the certificate must be ordered).
- Many original parish chest and poor law records remain physical-only at local record offices.

## Research tips
- Search the GRO civil death index (FreeBMD or FamilySearch's 1837-2007 Death Registration Index) first, by surname/quarter/year, then order the certificate for full detail.
- Cross-check the 1851 census (taken 30-31 March 1851) for the household shortly before a death that year, which can confirm age, birthplace, and address.
- Search parish burial registers for the likely parish, and note that Yorkshire collections are often split by Riding (North/East/West) rather than county-wide — check all applicable Ridings.
- Determine testate/intestate status before searching probate; pre-1858 Yorkshire probate sits in ecclesiastical court records, not the 1858+ National Probate Calendar.
- Check local newspapers (e.g. Yorkshire Gazette) for death notices or inquest reports.
- The FamilySearch Wiki pages fetched in this survey returned only generic template content for this locality; re-check the Wiki directly for Yorkshire/England-specific vital-records start dates and research tips before finalizing conclusions.
